summary: This informational RFC lists requirements for signaling inside a PCN domain. That includes carrying feedback from the egress node to the decision point and letting the decision point ask the ingress node to measure and report rates.

eli5.summary: The people watching the road need to tell the people at the gate what they see. This lists what that messaging system needs.

subtitle: Requirements for pre-congestion notification signaling in Diffserv networks.

tldr.problem: Diffserv domains need to protect quality of service for inelastic traffic (like VoIP and video) from being harmed by new flows, but the network cannot use standard reactive congestion control.
tldr.mechanism: Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN) marks packets at risk, and boundary nodes measure and report marked traffic rates to a decision point, which uses them to admit or reject new flows, and to terminate existing flows if needed.
tldr.outcome: PCN signaling must carry marked traffic rates from the edge to the decision point, and may need to allow the decision point to request measurements from ingress nodes, especially if the decision point is remote.

today: RFC 6663 is an Informational document defining signaling requirements for PCN. It remains current as the definitive specification of what PCN signaling protocols must carry.

sections.title: Quality of Service in Diffserv
sections.content: Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN) is a mechanism to protect quality of service for inelastic flows—like Voice over IP (VoIP), video conferencing, and streaming—within a Diffserv domain. PCN uses two techniques: admission control, which decides whether to admit a new flow request, and flow termination, which drops existing flows when the network is overloaded. The overall PCN architecture is defined in RFC 5559. This document specifies the signaling requirements needed for PCN to work: how information flows between the network edge and the decision points that make admission and termination decisions.
sections.eli5: The network watches for danger signs and tells a decision maker, who then says yes or no to new customers, or asks some current customers to leave.

sections.title: PCN Components and Operation
sections.content: PCN operates on three main components. PCN-boundary-nodes mark RTP or RTCP packets based on how much traffic they see. At PCN-egress-nodes (the exit points), the marked traffic is measured in regular intervals (typically 100 to 500 milliseconds). At the Decision Point, these measurements are used to make admission and termination decisions. The Decision Point may be collocated with a PCN-ingress-node (the entry point), in which case it has direct access to information, or it may be a centralized node. PCN supports two edge behaviors: Controlled Load (CL), which uses threshold marking and excess-traffic marking, and Single Marking (SM), which uses a single marking level. Each approach has different signaling requirements.
sections.eli5: Watch stations on the way out measure the load. A decision maker gets these counts. If they are far away, the entry point also has to send what it sent out, so the decision maker can compare.

sections.title: Feedback from the Network Edge
sections.content: The PCN-egress-node must report its measurements to the Decision Point regularly, typically at the end of each measurement interval, unless optional report suppression is enabled (in which case reports are sent less frequently if the network state is stable). For Single Marking (SM) mode, each report must contain the not-marked traffic rate (in octets per second) and the PCN-marked traffic rate. For Controlled Load (CL) mode, the report must include the not-marked rate, the threshold-marked rate, and the excess-traffic-marked rate. Both reports must identify the ingress and egress nodes to specify which path the measurement applies to. The report can be sent directly to the Decision Point or carried within another signaling message that passes through the egress node. To minimize signaling load, multiple reports for different paths can be combined in a single message. Signaling messages SHOULD be prioritized above regular PCN-traffic to ensure timely delivery.
sections.eli5: The edge sends counts of unmarked and marked cars every few seconds. If the decision maker is far away, it needs the ingress point's address too.

sections.title: Measurements from the Ingress Node
sections.content: When the Decision Point is not collocated with the PCN-ingress-node, the Decision Point may request the ingress node to measure and report the PCN-sent-rate—the total rate of PCN traffic sent toward a specific path. This signaling is only needed if the Decision Point and ingress node are separate. The request must specify the ingress and egress nodes that define the path, and the identity of the Decision Point requesting the measurement. The ingress node responds with the PCN-sent-rate in octets per second and the path identifiers. Since these requests are only sent when flow termination is urgently needed, they SHOULD be sent with high priority, low drop precedence, and in a reliable manner to ensure the message gets through.
sections.eli5: The decision maker can ask the entry point, 'How much are you sending down the road to exit point X?' and waits for an answer.

sections.title: Trust and Protection
sections.content: PCN signaling carries network management information that could disrupt service if spoofed or modified. The signaling between PCN-boundary-nodes must be protected from attacks. Messages must be authenticated so the recipient can verify that the sender is who it claims to be. The signaling should be protected against replay attacks (where an attacker replays an old message) and man-in-the-middle attacks (where an attacker intercepts and modifies messages). Possible mechanisms include digest authentication and encryption. For generic aggregate RSVP signaling (used in some deployments), RFC 4860 provides additional security methods. The specific security mechanisms are outside the scope of this requirements document; they are handled by the signaling protocol that carries PCN feedback.
sections.eli5: Make sure the person sending the counts is real, not someone pretending, and the counts have not been changed on the way.
